enonce_intro_markdown: Aluminium is prepared industrially from purified bauxite by electrolytic reduction.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Write the formula of the oxide.

(ii) Write the cathode half reaction for the process. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The oxide of aluminium electrolysed is aluminium oxide (alumina), **$\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$**, obtained by purifying bauxite and dissolved in molten cryolite.

(ii) At the cathode (negative electrode) aluminium ions gain electrons (reduction):

$\mathrm{Al^{3+}} + 3e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}$

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Can chemical reduction be used to extract Al from its ore?

(ii) Explain. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **No.**

(ii) Aluminium is **higher than carbon in the reactivity series** and its oxide is very stable (aluminium holds on to oxygen more strongly than carbon does). Carbon (or carbon monoxide) is therefore not a strong enough reducing agent to remove the oxygen from $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$, so the much more powerful method of electrolysis must be used.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i) Why are Al extraction plants usually located near power stations? *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: The electrolysis uses a **very large amount of electricity** (high current to keep the oxide molten and to deposit the metal). Siting the plant near a power station, usually a cheap hydroelectric one, reduces the cost of electricity and the cost of transmitting it, so production is cheaper.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give one large scale use of Al and relate this use to its property.

Use:

Property: *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Use:** overhead electric power cables (also: aircraft bodies, cooking pots, food foil).

**Property:** aluminium is a **good conductor of electricity and has a low density**, so the cables conduct well and are light enough to be carried by pylons. (For cooking pots the property would be good heat conduction; for aircraft, low density with strength.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State one metal that can be extracted by chemical reduction.

(ii) Name an ore from which this metal is extracted.

(iii) Write an equation for the extraction process. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Iron.**

(ii) **Haematite**, $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$ (magnetite, $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$, is another ore).

(iii) In the blast furnace carbon monoxide reduces the iron(III) oxide:

$\mathrm{Fe_2O_3} + 3\mathrm{CO} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe} + 3\mathrm{CO_2}$

(Check: left 2 Fe, 3 + 3 = 6 O, 3 C; right 2 Fe, 6 O, 3 C. Balanced.) Any other correct answer is accepted, for example zinc from zinc blende (after roasting) or lead from galena.
